newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says considering stiffer bank penalties.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says considering stiffer bank penalties.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is considering measures to strengthen the legal penalties against false reporting and evasion of inspections by banks, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Thursday.
"We are now considering ways to strengthen penalties under the banking law against evasion of inspections and false reporting," Mitsuzuka told a bankers' conference.

MOF will also strengthen inspection and supervision of the securities industry by boosting the functions of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), and by introducing stiffer penalties against insider trading, Mitsuzuka said.
Links to corporate racketeers, or sokaiya, have led to more than a dozen arrests of officials from Nomura Securities Co Ltd and one of Japan's biggest banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd.
Mitsuzuka said the incidents could result in the loss of credibility in the health and fairness of Japan's financial system both at home and abroad.
Financial firms must establish and embrace corporate morals and review their business management in order to prevent recurrences, he said.
MOF will request that the banking industry quickly consider ways to cut off links with corporate racketeers, he added.
Mitsuzuka stressed the importance of restructuring state finances so that the country's economy and society will be able to retain its vitality in the 21st century.
"We are now working to come up with bills for fiscal structural reforms for the next parliament session," he said.
